html:
The religion of the Fon, Ewe and related peoples of Benin and Togo, centred on spirits called vodun, who rule over parts of nature and society under a distant creator, Mawu-Lisa.

Worship involves shrines, offerings, drumming, dance and possession, and was organised in Dahomey under royal control. Enslaved people from this coast, shipped through Ouidah, carried it to the Americas, where it became Haitian Vodou and part of Brazilian Candomble. Missionaries and the Kerekou regime tried to suppress it, but since the 1990s Benin has honoured it with a national holiday each 10 January, centred on Ouidah. Many Beninese combine it with Christianity or Islam. See also the Haitian Revolution.
sum: The religion of the Fon, Ewe and related peoples of Benin and Togo, centred on spirits called vodun, who rule over parts of nature and society under a distant creator, Mawu-Lisa.
